mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP growth (GDPC1) above its 12-month moving average signals accelerating economic activity, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth exceeds its 12-month moving average but S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and corporate costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE falls below 4.5% but S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% but S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is falsified.
